items.q: Programmatic DOOH lets advertisers buy screen time through automated platforms.
items.why: Buyers use platforms to bid for plays on digital screens, much as they do for online ads.

items.q: A digital screen can change its ad by time of day or by weather.
items.why: That flexibility is one of the main strengths of digital out of home.

items.q: Proof of play shows that an ad was displayed on a screen at a given time.
items.why: It is the record buyers rely on to confirm their ad really ran.

items.q: An impression multiplier estimates how many people pass a screen for each play.
items.why: Because nobody clicks a billboard, audience is estimated from traffic and footfall.

items.q: Dwell time is how long people spend near a screen, and it can affect how long an ad should be.
items.why: In a queue people stay longer, so a longer spot can work. On a busy road, short is better.

items.q: Every DOOH venue plays ads of exactly the same length.
items.why: Spot lengths and loop lengths differ by venue and network.

items.q: A static poster can be changed instantly from a laptop.
items.why: A static poster has to be printed and put up. Only digital screens change instantly.

items.q: Share of voice on a screen is the share of the ad loop that a brand gets.
items.why: In a loop with five equal spots from different brands, each has a fifth.

items.q: Out-of-home audiences can only be measured by counting passing traffic.
items.why: Panels, anonymised sensors and location data are also used.

items.q: Location data can help show whether people who passed a screen later visited a store.
items.why: Advertisers use it to estimate store visits, though results are estimates.
